This diagonal is the line of symmetry, because it divides the kite into two congruent triangles that are mirror images of each other (the two equal sides on each side of the line match up exactly).
system_prompt:
You are an experienced scorer of the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. You score the responses to its constructed-response questions with each question's scoring guide, as TIMSS trains its scorers to do.

The figures of the test booklet are described in words, and test takers cannot draw, so they describe in words what they would draw, mark, shade, or write on a figure, graph, or table; score such a description as you would score the drawing it describes. Score only what the response says: when the scoring guide asks for work or an explanation, give no credit for work or reasoning that the response does not show. First explain briefly how the response compares with the scoring guide, then choose the category of the guide that the response belongs to.
user_prompt:
# Question

Draw the line of symmetry on this shape.

[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy-ends at either end.]

Figure, described in words:
A quadrilateral kite shape oriented diagonally on a blank background. It has a sharp, acute vertex pointing toward the bottom left. From this vertex, two long straight sides of equal length extend upward and to the right: one side goes steeply up and right to an upper vertex, and the other side goes gently up and right to a lower-right vertex. The top side is a short horizontal segment extending rightward from the upper vertex, and the right side is a short vertical segment extending upward from the lower-right vertex, meeting at a top-right corner.

# Scoring guide of the question (1 point)

- Correct Response (1 point):
  - Line drawn correctly as shown
[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy ends at either end. A dotted line goes lengthwise through the figure, through the pointy ends.]
- Incorrect Response (0 points):
  - Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

# Response to the question

Draw a straight line from the sharp acute vertex at the bottom left of the kite to the opposite vertex at the top-right corner, passing through the centre of the kite. This diagonal is the line of symmetry, because it divides the kite into two congruent triangles that are mirror images of each other (the two equal sides on each side of the line match up exactly).

Score the response to the question.
